findings.finding: The single most load-bearing safety mechanic in the whole architecture - the agent in-harness mutation interception round-trip (Claude can_use_tool / Codex item/commandExecution/requestApproval -> Gateway intent -> ActionRequest -> risk/preview -> approval -> allow|deny|REWRITE returned BACK to the harness) - has no dedicated sequence diagram. D1 is a generic pipeline flowchart + the canonical ActionExecution* event chain; D8 is the happy-path demo; D4 shows the adapter trait surface as two static lanes. None of them shows the synchronous callback round-trip where the harness BLOCKS waiting for the Gateway/human and receives an allow/deny/rewrite decision. This is exactly the 'hard mechanic that prose hides' the DIAGRAM_PLAN preamble says diagrams exist to clarify (ADR-006, AG 8/17). The prompt explicitly names 'can_use_tool->Gateway intercept' as a candidate that may need its own diagram - it does.
findings.evidence: DIAGRAM_PLAN.md D1 (lines 21-25) 'must show the ordered pipeline ... + the canonical event chain' - a flowchart + event-chain sequenceDiagram, neither of which has a harness lifeline or the return value to the harness. D4 (lines 39-43) is 'Mermaid flowchart (two lanes converging)' - static, not a round-trip. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 4.2 law #1 and 9.1 call can_use_tool 'the in-harness mutation chokepoint (allow/deny/rewrite -> Gateway intent)'; ACTION_GATEWAY.md 5.5 (Agent Session Adapters) + 8 lifecycle confirm this is a distinct actor path. No D entry has an agent/harness lifeline blocking on the Gateway decision.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a new P0 sequence diagram (call it D1a or fold into an expanded D1) in ARCHITECTURE.md 19: lifelines = Agent (Claude SDK / Codex app-server), HarnessAdapter, Gateway, Approval/HumanInputQueue, EventStore. Show the SYNCHRONOUS path: agent attempts tool/command -> adapter intercept-mutation -> Gateway normalize/risk/preview -> (auto-allow at risk<=1 | ApprovalRequested at risk>=2) -> human decision -> allow|deny|REWRITE returned to the adapter -> agent proceeds/blocked, with ActionExecution* events emitted only by the Gateway. Anchor to AG 8/15.1/17, ADR-006, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 9.1.

findings.finding: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 19 ('Diagrams') and DIAGRAM_PLAN.md disagree on which diagrams are the build-critical / embedded set. 19 enumerates a flat list of 8 'Priority diagrams' with NO P0/P1/P2 distinction: (1) system map=D0, (2) Gateway pipeline=D1, (3) 4 canonical chains=D5, (4) session lifecycle=D3, (5) event/projection/outbox=D2, (6) adapter seam=D4, (7) Brain seam=D7, (8) demo=D8. But DIAGRAM_PLAN declares the P0 (build-critical) set as exactly {D0, D1, D2, D3, D8} and puts D4/D5/D7 at P1. So 19 silently promotes three P1 diagrams (D4, D5, D7) into its 'priority' list while OMITTING D6 (trust boundaries) - which the plan ALSO marks P1 and even flags for possible Excalidraw promotion. The two documents give a finalizer two different answers to 'which diagrams must be embedded in the binding ARCHITECTURE.md.'
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md 19 lists 8 diagrams as 'Priority diagrams' flat. DIAGRAM_PLAN.md lines 83-86: 'P0 (build-critical): D0, D1, D2, D3, D8 | P1 (clarify seams): D4, D5, D6, D7 | P2: D9, D10.' The prompt's own framing ('are the P0 diagrams D0/D1/D2/D3/D8 the right set to embed') matches the plan, not 19. D6 appears in the plan's P1 but is absent from 19's list entirely.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md 19, replace the flat 'Priority diagrams' enumeration with the DIAGRAM_PLAN's explicit tiering (P0 build-critical = D0/D1/D2/D3/D8 embedded inline; P1 = D4/D5/D6/D7; P2 = D9/D10), and state explicitly which tiers are embedded vs linked. Reconcile the D5/D4/D7 promotion (either keep them P1-and-linked or justify embedding) and restore D6 to the list. Single source of truth = DIAGRAM_PLAN.

findings.finding: The fencing-token correctness mechanic has no diagram that actually shows it working, despite being a LOCKED, mandatory invariant (ADR-008) and named explicitly in the prompt. The plan reduces it to a single line-item inside two flowcharts: D1 'fencing-token check' (one box in a pipeline) and D9 'lease reclaim + new fencing token on restart.' Neither shows the failure scenario the mechanic exists to prevent: a paused-then-resumed STALE session presents an OLD fencing token to the Gateway, the Gateway REJECTS its write, protecting the worktree that a NEW session (which reclaimed the expired lease with a NEW, higher token) now owns. This is precisely the subtle correctness path DATA_MODEL 2.6 describes in prose, and it is invisible as a one-word flowchart node.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md 2.6: 'an executor must present its lease fencing_token to the gateway, which rejects any write whose token is older than the current lease holder - this is the protection against a paused-then-resumed stale session clobbering a worktree another session now owns. ... reclamation mints a NEW token, invalidating the old holder.' DIAGRAM_PLAN D1 (line 23) lists 'fencing-token check' as one item; D9 (line 71) lists 'lease reclaim + new fencing token.' No diagram has two competing session timelines + the Gateway rejection.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a small sequenceDiagram (embed in D1's section or as a D9 sub-panel, promote to P1) showing: SessionA acquires lease (token=5) on worktree -> SessionA pauses/stalls -> lease expires -> SessionB reclaims (token=6) -> SessionA resumes and attempts a write with token=5 -> Gateway rejects (stale token) -> SessionA fenced off. Anchor to ADR-008, DATA_MODEL 2.6, AG 16.2/16.4.

findings.finding: The resume-or-replay survival mechanic (ADR-010), called out by the prompt as one of the riskiest mechanics and acknowledged in the docs as 'the genuinely fragile part,' is parked at P2 (D9) and therefore would NOT be embedded in the binding ARCHITECTURE.md P0 set. The daemon-restart recovery path - reconstruct projections by replay -> reconcile live git2 -> ping Brain -> reclaim leases + mint new fencing tokens -> resume harness (claude --resume / codex thread/resume) ELSE serialized-scrollback replay + relaunch - is a multi-branch decision flow that prose buries across ADR-010, DATA_MODEL 7.2, and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 12. Its priority (P2) does not match its risk/complexity. D9 also bundles three distinct scenarios (UI restart, daemon restart, orphan kill) into one entry, which will produce a cramped diagram for the highest-risk path.
findings.evidence: DIAGRAM_PLAN.md D9 (lines 69-73) priority 'P2'; 'Format: Mermaid sequenceDiagram (restart scenarios) + stateDiagram for the runner.' DECISIONS.md ADR-010 rationale: 'True live-process survival across a full daemon crash is the genuinely fragile part (R-PTY) ... Accurate alt-screen/raw-mode TUI re-attach is lossy.' DATA_MODEL.md 7.2 'Recovery on daemon restart (ADR-010)' lists 5 reconcile steps. The prompt names 'resume-or-replay survival' as a hard mechanic needing a diagram.
findings.proposed_fix: Promote the daemon-restart resume-or-replay path to P1 (or split D9 into D9a 'daemon-restart recovery' P1 + D9b 'UI-restart reconnect / orphan kill' P2). The P1 diagram must show the resume-vs-replay BRANCH per harness and the lease-reclaim/new-fencing-token step. Anchor to ADR-010, DATA_MODEL 7.2, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 12.

findings.finding: No diagram covers a failure/degraded path end-to-end; every diagram is a happy path. The architecture's distinctive correctness guarantees - projection crash-recovery (interrupt mid-apply -> replay -> consistent), degraded-projection handling (mark degraded, skip bad event, never corrupt raw events), fail-closed-on-audit-write, and Brain graceful degradation when absent/stale - are all tested invariants (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 14) but appear only as one-line annotations inside D2/D7. For an event-sourced system whose whole pitch is crash-recoverability and fail-closed auditing, the absence of any recovery/degraded diagram is a coverage gap, though lower priority than the safety/fencing/survival mechanics.
findings.evidence: DIAGRAM_PLAN D2 (line 29) lists 'projection rebuild path (replay events WHERE seq > last_seq)' as one item in a flowchart; no crash-interrupt branch. DATA_MODEL 7.2 specifies three recovery modes (startup replay / full rebuild / degraded-skip). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 14 tests 'crash-recovery (interrupt mid-apply -> replay -> consistent)' and 'fail-closed-on-audit-write' - neither is diagrammed. EM 13.2 'projection corruption must not corrupt raw events.'
findings.proposed_fix: Either add a small recovery sub-panel to D2 (startup-replay vs full-rebuild vs degraded-skip branches, with the in-txn offset-advance crash boundary marked) or note in DIAGRAM_PLAN that the resume-or-replay D9 diagram covers the daemon-level recovery and D2 must include the projection-level crash-interrupt branch. Anchor to DATA_MODEL 7.2, EM 13.2.

findings.finding: DIAGRAM_PLAN D3 (session lifecycle) names a '16-state' Session machine, but DATA_MODEL 4.1 and SESS-3 (PRD 10.4) enumerate the canonical state set and the count is ambiguous/inconsistent across docs - the diagram plan asserts a specific cardinality the upstream specs do not cleanly support, which will surface as a drift question when the diagram is drawn. DATA_MODEL 4.1 groups states into base/runtime-sub/waiting-sub/terminal without giving a single canonical count; PRD SESS-3 lists 16 status tokens but ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 4.1 also references '16 states' loosely. A stateDiagram-v2 forces an exact node count, so this latent ambiguity must be resolved before D3 is drawn.
findings.evidence: DIAGRAM_PLAN.md D3 (line 34): 'how a session moves through its 16 states.' PRD 10.4 SESS-3 lists: creating, starting, active, thinking, running_command, editing_files, running_tests, waiting_on_permission, waiting_on_human, waiting_on_external_service, idle, stale, failed, changes_ready, completed, archived, killed (= 17 tokens). DATA_MODEL 4.1 uses 'waiting_on_human_input' (vs PRD 'waiting_on_human') and presents states as base+sub-states, not a flat 16. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT 5 says '8 status state machines' and 4.1 caption '(16 states)'.
findings.proposed_fix: Before drawing D3, reconcile the exact Session state set across PRD SESS-3 / DATA_MODEL 4.1 / UX 8.1 (and the waiting_on_human vs waiting_on_human_input naming) and state the authoritative count in ARCHITECTURE.md 5/19. The D3 stateDiagram must match that reconciled enum exactly. (This is the D02/D03 state-machine reconciliation already flagged in 23 item 3.)
